rationale: The diagnostic run 0ebe4472b71d4f82b0303807b2875549 narrows the gap: node 5 is following leader 2 but is still in Phase::Prepare with promise ballot (n=2,pid=2), while node 2 is in Accept at decided 4, so no AcceptSync was applied to node 5. Whether the leader generated it is still unobserved; the successor adds queue-level flags for the Promise, the AcceptSync and node 5's Accepted reply.

gaps.question: Were a Promise from node 5, an AcceptSync to node 5, and an Accepted reply from node 5 actually produced and routed after node 5's late Prepare?

interpretations.rationale: The sampled state identifies where the predicted step fails but not why. Event 0 (ready) again establishes the premise: leader 1 decided 5, node 2 decided 4 with accepted 5, and node 5 decided 5 with index 4 reading decided. Event 1 (after_sync) reports node 5 decided 5 and regressed=false, and the diagnostics place node 5 in Phase::Prepare (n5_accept=false) with its promise at ballot n=2,pid=2, while node 2 is in the Accept phase (n2_accept=true) at decided 4 and node 5's leader view is pid 2. So node 5 did accept the new leader's Prepare and did promise it, but no AcceptSync was applied: the phase never advanced to Accept and the decided index never moved. The source path handle_promise_accept -> send_accsync -> handle_acceptsync -> sync_log would have set decided 4 and moved node 5 to Accept if the leader had handled the Promise in Accept and the follower had accepted the AcceptSync. The remaining possibilities are that node 2 never generated the AcceptSync for this Promise, or that it was generated but not routed to node 5 by the probe, or that node 5's ballot or phase guard rejected it (its recorded promise ballot matches the new leader, so a guard rejection is unlikely but unverified). The next run records whether a Promise from 5, an AcceptSync to 5, and an Accepted reply from 5 actually appear in the message queue.
counterevidence: Node 2 being in Accept at decided 4 and node 5 promising at the same ballot shows the leader-side precondition was met, so the missing step is later in the chain than the prepare quorum.
This run still does not show the target violating anything: node 5's decided index was not lowered, so the receipt neither supports the claim nor establishes a protection.
limitations: Node 5's phase is inferred from get_current_leader's Accept flag; internal phase Recover and Prepare cannot be distinguished through the public API.
Queue-level presence of the three messages is not yet recorded; the next run adds it.

scope.description: Same five-node selective-delivery scenario, with queue-level observation of the Promise, AcceptSync and Accepted messages around node 5's late promise.
assumptions: Messages are delivered only along the routes each step names; withheld messages stay queued.
No ticks are called, so leadership is obtained only through try_become_leader.
excluded: Snapshots, flexible quorums, batching, reconfiguration and multiple delayed promises.

experiment.prefix: Identical construction to the previous run: decide Value(1..=4) on all nodes; append Value(5), deliver its AcceptDecide to 2,3,5 and purge it for 4, deliver the Accepteds to node 1, deliver the Decide only to node 5; emit ready. Cut node 1; elect node 2 with promises from 3 and 4 only; hold node 2's Prepare for node 5; deliver the AcceptSyncs to 3 and 4 and hold their Accepted replies. Deliver the held Prepare to node 5, collect and record promise_seen, route the Promise to node 2, collect and record acceptsync_seen, route the AcceptSync, collect and record n5_accepted_reply, then emit late_sync phase=after_sync with decided, decided_before, entry_status, decided_leader2, regressed, n5_leader_pid, n5_accept, n5_promise_n, n5_promise_pid, n2_accept, promise_seen, acceptsync_seen, n5_accepted_reply. Then deliver the held Accepted replies, settle among nodes 2..5, and emit after_redecide.

comparisons.description: The leader produced an AcceptSync addressed to node 5 after the late Promise.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds three queue-level flags sampled around the late promise: whether node 5 emitted a Promise, whether an AcceptSync addressed to node 5 appeared after the Promise was routed to the leader, and whether node 5 emitted an Accepted reply after the AcceptSync was routed. Scenario, delivery control and all previously sampled fields are unchanged.
